//: GATE MANIFEST — read by .repl/gate.py. One row per instrument that protects something.
//path: path is relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT (the folder that holds paracore/, paracore-gen/, ...), not to paracore/.
//cwd: cwd is the directory the gate must run in. Set to what was MEASURED to work, not what looks right.
//python: 'auto' = the interpreter running gate.py. Any other value is a key in gate.py's VENVS table.
//runs: 'auto' = runs unattended in every gate run. 'manual' = declared but NOT run, and why_not_auto must say why.
//known_red: An allowance. Requires why + remedy + blocked_by + owner. It is CLEARED (and the run FAILS) the moment the gate goes green, so a stale allowance cannot survive.

gates.protects: No tracked file still names a symbol we removed (RETIRED.md). This is the gate that makes a removal actually finish.
The injected MEMORY.md fits its own stated budget, its end sentinel is intact, and every APPENDIX anchor it cites resolves.
Every ```csharp fence in every MCP skill tree still COMPILES. A skill is prose that nothing else type-checks, so a bad recipe otherwise costs every agent that follows it.
The generated AI instruction tree still carries every rule from paracore/ai/ — a regeneration must not silently drop one.
The chart/REPL API surface the engine promises still exists after a refactor.
Every extension method the engine actually declares is documented in EXTENSION_METHODS.md — an undocumented member is invisible to the AI.
The generated EXTENSION_METHODS index is DERIVED from source, not hand-edited — a second parser must agree, and a mutation must be picked up.
The shipped copies of the generated engine docs match what gen-engine-docs.py produces — no hand-edit drift.
Every REPL hover doc PARSES and loses no word. A self-closing <see cref="X"/> inside a <summary> contributes no text, so the tooltip silently reads a word short.
The sentinel (watchdog) surface is taught exactly where a script can write it, and is invisible everywhere else.
No MCP prompt or skill teaches a Paracore method the engine does not have. The MCPs reach Revit over gRPC, so this coupling is TEXT and the compiler can never see it.
The SessionGate consent dialog stays INVISIBLE to the modal-dialog watcher — its button labels must never intersect the watcher's KEEP/DISCARD sets.
Every unit the engine CONVERTS also has a canonical DISPLAY suffix. Two hand-maintained switches over one vocabulary; one can drift.
The add-in Revit will actually load is the build on disk. Every conclusion drawn from a running Revit is worthless if it was drawn against an older build.
The frozen MCP exes contain the CURRENT mcp_core. An exe is a frozen snapshot: a .py edit does nothing until it is rebuilt AND installed, and nothing errors.
WORKSPACE_MAP.md matches what is actually on disk and what the remotes actually hold. A map nothing checks is a map that lies.

known_red.why: paracore-business and paracore-gallery are each 1 commit ahead of origin. The commits made on 2026-10-27 exist only on this machine.
known_red.remedy: Push the two repos, or confirm the commits are meant to stay local.
known_red.blocked_by: Pushing is the user's call; nothing was pushed when the 2026-10-27 commits were made.

gates.protects: Every gallery script obeys the pack file policy, and the policy's own canaries still fire.
A capture/diff pair over the live takeoff output, so a change to one section is provable not to have moved any other.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs a LIVE Revit session with the engine add-in loaded; there is no model to read otherwise.

gates.protects: Runs a test file's bodies without a pytest SESSION (a pytest run rotates %TEMP% and is a delete).
gates.why_not_auto: Takes a test file as an argument; a bare run has nothing to prove, so it must not be counted as green.

gates.protects: Proves the sentinel-surface gate can actually FAIL, by mutating the real file and restoring it byte-for-byte.
gates.why_not_auto: It MUTATES the real tree. Run it deliberately after changing the sentinel surface, never in a batch.

gates.protects: Runs the MCP's own anti-pattern checks over a C# file, so a probe is fixed before it is sent.
gates.why_not_auto: Takes .cs paths. It is a per-file linter, not a repo-wide assertion.

gates.protects: Every prompt the assembler reads at runtime is actually inside the frozen exe.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs <exe> <prompts_dir>. A bare run prints usage and exits 0, so treating it as an auto gate would report green while checking nothing.

gates.protects: All nine skills are inside the frozen exe, so read_skill() cannot answer 'No skill named ...'.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs the built exe path; it is invoked by build-gen.ps1 after the build.

gates.protects: The export_view tool survives FastMCP decoration with its -> Image annotation intact.
gates.why_not_auto: Imports mcp_server.py, which needs the build venv AND the built exe; it is a build-time spike.

gates.protects: The FilteredElementCollector / get_Parameter lint narrowing does not fire on correct family-authoring code.
gates.why_not_auto: A one-off regression probe for a 2026-10-02 change; it has no pass/fail contract to assert on every run.

gates.protects: The family MCP's runtime prompts are inside its frozen exe.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs the built exe path; invoked by build-family.ps1 after the build.

gates.protects: spec_preview and drawing_reader — both imported INSIDE a function body — are actually in the frozen exe. That is exactly the shape PyInstaller drops without failing the build.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs the built exe path; invoked by build-model.ps1 after the build.

gates.protects: The model MCP's runtime prompts are inside its frozen exe.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs the built exe path; invoked by build-model.ps1 after the build.

gates.protects: Proves the raster gate can fail rather than silently passing an empty scan.
gates.why_not_auto: A teeth prover: it mutates state to prove the gate bites, so it is run deliberately.

gates.protects: Description-embedded counts agree with the audit sheet, and audit totals agree with the status report — the D22 class of defect.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs an exported BOQ workbook to read; there is nothing to check until an export has run.

gates.protects: The rate matcher resolves the real BOQ row descriptions it is meant to price.
gates.why_not_auto: Needs openpyxl and the exported BOQ workbook; it reports an environment error, not a verdict, without them.
